races.name: Killik Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sky Secret
runners_data.note: C&D winner with a recent good-ground win (1/5f/GOO) and consistent form at 5f; Rossa Ryan partners a horse who wants to dominate from the front, and on good ground at Sandown she has the strongest front-running credentials in the field.
runners_data.comment: Sky Secret showed a win four starts back and returns on a sharp 11-day turnaround carrying 136 lb from stall 4, with experience over today's trip and a rating of 91 suggesting he holds strong claims — the risk is that he has been out of the frame in his last three starts.

runners_data.name: Innichen
runners_data.note: William Buick takes the ride on a horse with two recent wins (6f and 5f on good ground) and a strong RPR of 135; a genuine hold-up type who needs pace to close into, and this contested early gallop is exactly the scenario that suits his profile.
runners_data.comment: Innichen showed his class when winning two of his last six starts, with a third two outings back keeping him in good heart before an unplaced effort last time; he has experience over today's trip and going, and 135 lb from stall two makes him one to respect here.

runners_data.name: Undercover Affair
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane on a David Evans-trained runner with a sharp T14 strike rate (1/8) who has proven 5f good-ground form including a win; a natural prominent racer who will travel just off the pace and is dangerous if he can stick to the inside rail at Sandown.
runners_data.comment: Undercover Affair arrives here on the back of a win three starts back, and his experience over today's trip and conditions is a clear asset carrying 131 lb from stall five; the risk is that his last two outings have yielded only a fifth and an eighth.

runners_data.name: Betty Boop
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy partners a Richard Hughes-trained filly with a small but solid form profile (1W2P from 3 runs) entirely on good ground; a hold-up type who drops back to 5f from 7f and will need the pace to be genuine to deliver her finishing effort.
runners_data.comment: A winner two starts back and third three starts back, Betty Boop arrives in decent nick on 20 days' rest, has run over today's trip, and our rating of 83 supports her claims; the fifth last time out is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Rotelle
runners_data.note: Wears headgear (p) for the first time and has a C&D win (1/5f/GOO) in recent form; a prominent type for Charlie Fellowes who handles good ground well and could benefit if she settles sweetly and produces a clean turn of foot inside the final furlong.
runners_data.comment: Rotelle ran well to finish second last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, but that eighth two starts back is a blot, and carrying 128 lb from stall three while ranked fifth of eight on ratings suggests he faces a stiff task here.

runners_data.name: Arabica Queen
runners_data.note: Steps down in trip to 5f from her 6f best, which is a concern for her ability to dominate early; a confirmed front-runner who risks being drawn into a pace battle with Sky Secret that leaves both vulnerable to the closers arriving late.
runners_data.comment: Arabica Queen comes into this off a 28-day break with experience over today's trip, and a win three starts back shows she can find the winner's enclosure, though she was unplaced last time and ranks sixth of eight on our ratings, so she faces a stiff task from stall one carrying 123 lb.

runners_data.name: Holi Scarlett
runners_data.note: Sean Levey partners a consistent prominent type with seven runs on good/similar ground (1W4P) who rarely runs a bad race at 5f; Stuart Williams has a decent T14 (4/34) and Levey will look to slot in just off the leaders and grind through the final climb.
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Holi Scarlett faces a stiff ask, though she does offer some encouragement — third last time out, and a winner four starts back, with experience over today's trip and going and a 27-day break suggesting she returns fresh.

runners_data.name: True Charm
runners_data.note: Lemos De Souza's runner has only one place from three runs and hasn't raced in 49 days, representing a meaningful freshness risk; naturally a prominent racer, its position in midfield reflects the overcrowded forward berths rather than preference, making it hard to win from a role it hasn't needed to fill before.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, True Charm faces a stiff ask here; a return to today's going and a second three starts back offer slim encouragement, but 49 days off the track adds another question mark.

races.paceDynamic: Sky Secret and Arabica Queen are confirmed front-runners who will contest the lead from the gates, creating a genuinely competitive early pace over Sandown's stiff 5f on good ground. Sky Secret (Rossa Ryan) has the stronger recent speed figures and a win over this course and distance, while Arabica Queen drops back in trip from her 6f form and is likely to press rather than dominate. The resulting honest, pressure-filled gallop means the race will be run at a true tempo throughout, with very little let-up over the final two furlongs where Sandown's rise tests stamina. This shape suits prominent-to-midfield horses with a strong finish rather than pure front-runners, as the early battle between the two leaders risks leaving them vulnerable late — hold-up types with proven ability to close on good ground stand to benefit most. This field carries more forward-leaning runners than can all secure a prominent berth; Sky Secret is best-placed to dominate from the rail, while Arabica Queen is most likely to be the one crowded out and forced to settle slightly off the pace than her natural style demands.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Sky Secret and Arabica Queen burn each other off at honest pace, leaving the field strung out and vulnerable to a strong finisher.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners set a genuine gallop that plays into the hands of hold-up and midfield horses with finishing speed, particularly over Sandown's testing climb home. Innichen and Betty Boop, both proven finishers on good ground with strong RPR profiles, are ideally positioned to swoop late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Sky Secret clears the field early and Arabica Queen fails to sustain her challenge, allowing an uncontested leader to control fractions.
scenarios.body: Sky Secret has the class, the Sandown C&D win in her recent form, and Rossa Ryan's positional intelligence to steal a march on the field if Arabica Queen drops away. A solo leader over 5f on good ground who controls the tempo is notoriously hard to reel in, and Sky Secret's OR-86 rating underlines the ceiling she holds.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Grinders Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest but not scorching, allowing the prominent stalkers to travel smoothly and pounce just inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Undercover Affair and Rotelle, both genuine prominent types with strong good-ground records over 5f, are well-suited to sitting just off a solid gallop and hitting the line running. Billy Loughnane on Undercover Affair brings a live trainer angle (Evans T14: 1/8) that adds weight to this shape delivering for the chasing pack.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Sweep Falls Short
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the field fans wide, reducing the advantage of hold-up horses who need a strong tempo to close.
scenarios.body: Betty Boop and Innichen are true closers who require genuine pace to exploit, and any slowdown in fractions over 5f leaves them too much to do at the furlong pole. True Charm, naturally a prominent racer pushed to midfield by the race shape, is unlikely to get the gaps it needs and its redistribution tag further dilutes this scenario's probability.

watchPoints.text: Sky Secret and Arabica Queen — monitor the first furlong to see which secures the rail and which is forced to concede position; if Arabica Queen is pushed back from her natural lead role, she becomes vulnerable and the whole race shape tilts toward the closers.

Innichen (William Buick) — top jockey on a horse with two recent wins and strong pace figures; if Buick gets a clean run through on the inside rail in the closing stages, this hold-up horse has the RPR (135) to threaten any scenario.

True Charm — 49 days off the track and racing out of its natural prominent position due to pace congestion; watch in-running for signs of it getting trapped in traffic or failing to pick up from deeper than usual.

Rotelle (headgear) — first-time hood for Charlie Fellowes' filly; headgear debuts on two-year-olds on good ground at sprint trips can produce sharp responses, and her C&D win gives her course confidence worth monitoring in the market moves pre-race.

Betty Boop — stepping back from 7f to 5f is a notable drop in trip for a hold-up filly; watch how she travels in the early stages to assess whether she has the natural pace to be competitive at this distance under Murphy.

races.name: Killik Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: South Shore
runners_data.note: Strong hold-up performer with wins at five furlongs on good; Marco Ghiani has a clear brief to come late, and four days since last run suggests freshness, but must overcome a field shape that won't guarantee a strong pace to aim at.
runners_data.comment: South Shore has been a model of consistency, placed in each of his last six starts with wins four and five starts back, and he has raced over today's distance and going before; the concern is whether four days is enough recovery time carrying 138 lb.

runners_data.name: Good Earth
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type whose recent form includes a win and a second from 15 runs on similar going, though a run 18 lengths back last time on good makes that strike rate misleading; Connor Planas picks up the ride with trainer posting 3/14 at the current meeting.
runners_data.comment: Good Earth is our top-rated runner and arrives fresh on 15 days' rest, carrying 138 lb from stall 7, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour. Winless in his last six starts, but a second four starts back hints at better, and an rating of 80 makes him the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Duskaura
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who drops from six to five furlongs after a recent win at six on good; William Carson partners for Tony Carroll who has been active at this meeting (3/37 strike rate), and the hold-up style suits a race where late pace may arrive, but the step back in trip is a small concern.
runners_data.comment: Duskaura arrives here on the back of a win two starts ago and has experience of today's trip and going, with a rating of 77 suggesting she holds strong claims against this field; the risk is that eighth last time out leaves a question mark over her current form.

runners_data.name: Hint Of Humour
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent racer who has placed second three times at five furlongs on good or standard — the record suits this flat five-furlong track; Rossa Ryan takes over after a 66-day break, and that freshness combined with the front-pack position makes this a key profile to watch if Level Up weakens late.
runners_data.comment: Hint Of Humour returns third last time out and has placed second on three occasions in recent starts, giving her a strong profile as a danger here, though a 66-day absence and a winless run in her last six starts are the risks to weigh.

runners_data.name: Maharajas Express
runners_data.note: An authentic hold-up horse — won at five furlongs on good in recent form — but the crowded rear means he is realistically mapping into midfield rather than his preferred back-of-the-field position; Billy Loughnane must find a route through a likely wall of horses with STYLE_FIT of 0.90 tempering confidence.
runners_data.comment: Maharajas Express won two starts back but has otherwise struggled in recent starts, finishing sixth or worse on four occasions in that spell; he has run over today's trip and going, and 135 lb is no easy ask, though an 11-day turnaround suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Level Up
runners_data.note: The only confirmed pace-setter, equipped with a hood (headgear) and ridden by Oisin Murphy who knows how to control from the front; five places from six runs at five furlongs on good or soft underlines his consistency, and David Evans sends him in on a tight 22-day turnaround suggesting readiness.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win two starts back but has since slipped to sixth, and while he has run over today's trip and going, the 135 lb burden from stall nine may test his ability to recapture that form against stronger company.

runners_data.name: Cameley Days
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner wearing a tongue-tie who has placed four times from nine runs on good going at five furlongs; Lewis Edmunds rides for a trainer who has yet to fire at this meeting (0/7 in 14 days), though the tactical position travelling just off Level Up gives him every chance if the pace is sane.
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Cameley Days has struggled for consistency in recent starts, with just one win in her last six and back-to-back disappointing efforts latest; a third three starts back offers little encouragement, though she has distance and going experience and returns fit on 14 days' rest.

runners_data.name: Jenny Jerome
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up filly returning from a long 125-day break — the extended absence is the most significant flag here; naturally a back-of-the-field type, she is effectively displaced into midfield by this congested field structure, and Alistair Rawlinson will need significant luck in running given the combination of race-fitness doubts and positional compromise.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Jenny Jerome faces a stiff task here, though she has run over today's trip and going before and did finish second two starts back — a small crumb of comfort after 125 days off the track.

runners_data.name: So Smart
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer who won at five furlongs on good recently and has placed in six of 15 similar-going runs; wearing a hood and a tongue-piece, and trained by Grace Harris (3/14 at this meeting), but Laura Coughlan's 3lb claim counts for less when the horse's natural style is squeezed out of its ideal slot at STYLE_FIT of 0.94.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of nine on our figures and his recent form has been patchy, with a seventh last time out clouding an earlier win three starts back; he has run over today's trip and going, and stall one is a neutral fact, but 130 lb makes the task no easier.

races.paceDynamic: Level Up is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Oisin Murphy can dictate terms at a controlled, honest gallop on good ground over five furlongs at Sandown. Hint Of Humour and Cameley Days will push forward from the prominent berths to track Level Up, creating a two-or-three-horse lead group but not an explosive early pace that would set the race up for closers. The field actually contains more hold-up types than can occupy rear positions naturally — Maharajas Express, Jenny Jerome, and So Smart have all been redistributed to midfield on the map because the pack is too large to accommodate them all at the back, meaning they are likely racing fractionally out of their ideal role. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with tactical speed and a late burst, but given Level Up's uncontested lead and the genuine possibility of a front-runner dictating a moderate tempo, prominent racers travelling smoothly behind the pace — particularly those with strong good-ground form at five furlongs — are the principal beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Level Up Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Level Up finds an uncontested lead and Murphy controls fractions at a comfortable gallop.
scenarios.body: Level Up strides into his favoured role with nothing to chase him, conserving energy through the first three furlongs before quickening off a strong cruising pace; his record of five places in six runs at five furlongs on good shows he handles this setup well. Prominent runners Hint Of Humour and Cameley Days who track him without cover get first run off the turn and are ideally placed to capitalise if Level Up ties up late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Hint Of Humour or Cameley Days travels strongest in behind and sweeps past Level Up inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A competitive gallop from Level Up stretches the field, but Hint Of Humour — who has an excellent second-place record on good ground at five furlongs — sits a length off the pace before producing a strong late drive; Cameley Days, wearing a tongue-tie and fresh from placing form on this course-and-distance combination, offers similar coverage from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Storm Through
scenarios.trigger: If Level Up sets a genuinely quick early pace that brings the field back to the closers in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: South Shore, a proven finisher who has won twice at five furlongs on good ground and is drawn with a clear late-run in mind, benefits most from any collapse in the lead group; Duskaura, a three-year-old with a recent six-furlong win on good going, has the pace to thread through and represent the Tony Carroll yard on a sharp track.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos — Midfield Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the reshuffled hold-up horses Maharajas Express, Jenny Jerome, and So Smart fail to settle in their compromised midfield positions and the race fragments.
scenarios.body: Racing out of their natural roles, Maharajas Express and So Smart in particular may hang wider than ideal and fail to find the split they need in a tight five-furlong sprint; in this scenario the horses already correctly positioned — Level Up and the prominent pair — dominate the finish regardless, with any hold-up winner requiring significant luck in running.

watchPoints.text: Level Up (Murphy) — watch whether he gets a clean, uncontested lead in the early strides; if Cameley Days or Hint Of Humour push up hard to his girth in the first furlong the pace dynamic changes significantly.

Maharajas Express and Jenny Jerome — both are true hold-up horses racing in compromised midfield positions; monitor their settling behaviour in the early exchanges as fighting for position could cost them the energy they need for a late challenge.

Jenny Jerome — 125 days off the track is a serious fitness question mark in a sharp five-furlong sprint on good ground; watch her pre-race demeanour and market movement for signs connections believe she is race-ready.

South Shore — four days since last run is a very quick turnaround; Robert Cowell's horse ran twice in close succession earlier in the form string, so watch for any sign of below-par early pace in the stall, which would indicate the return has come too soon.

Hint Of Humour — 66-day layoff for a prominent racer who needs to travel fluently from the gate; if she shows any hesitation leaving the stalls or is caught flat-footed she will be shuffled back and lose the tactical position that defines her best chance.

races.name: House Of Killik Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Hungarian
runners_data.note: Progressive 3yo for Lemos De Souza who won last time at Sandown over 7f and steps up to 8f here on going he handles; sits prominently which is ideal in this shape, and the step in trip looks well timed on his trajectory.
runners_data.comment: Hungarian arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going before, giving him a solid profile heading in; carrying 137 lb from stall five is the one query, but at a rating of 92 he looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Home Hero
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner whose back-to-back wins at this trip on good ground give him strong course-and-distance credentials, but he runs just two days after his last start and Luke Catton's claim removes some weight; the key question is whether he can repel Thursday Girl for the early lead.
runners_data.comment: Home Hero won two starts back but was well beaten last time out, and at just two days since his last run, freshness must be a question mark; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 135 lb from stall seven, and faces a competitive field ranked fifth of eight.

runners_data.name: Magic Trip
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's hold-up performer returns from 77 days off and drops back to a mile he has not tackled since finishing third at Sandown; that placed effort on the mile is encouraging but the layoff and recent poor form figures (5-10-5) temper enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Magic Trip arrives with distance and going experience to call on and catches the eye on a rating of 81, yet he is winless in his last five starts and that fifth-placed effort last time out after a 77-day absence leaves improvement needed to land this.

runners_data.name: Thursday Girl
runners_data.note: Relentlessly consistent filly who has been placed in five of her last six starts including a win over this course and trip; Oisin Murphy takes over and she will press for the early lead, making her an obvious danger whether she wins the pace battle or settles just off it.
runners_data.comment: Thursday Girl returns in fair heart after winning two starts back, though her recent record shows four runner-up finishes in her last five, suggesting she finds one too good; she has experience over today's trip and going, but the 132 lb is a stiff ask from stall six.

runners_data.name: Drymee
runners_data.note: Has won twice from five starts over a mile on good ground and Billy Loughnane rode her to one of those wins; natural hold-up performer whose chance depends on a strong gallop being maintained — the crowded backfield may limit her ability to find a clear run entering the straight.
runners_data.comment: Drymee won back-to-back two and three starts back, has form over today's trip and going, and steps into the plate fresh enough at 20 days since his third last time out; the weight burden of 132 lb from stall four is the one factor to weigh up.

runners_data.name: Dovecote
runners_data.note: Relatively unexposed Ralph Beckett filly with only three starts, all placed at 7f-8f; Rossa Ryan takes the ride and she races prominently, meaning the honest pace plays directly to her style if she can handle the step into handicap company.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with two runner-up finishes doing little to disguise a modest speed rating of 63, Dovecote faces a stiff task from stall eight carrying 131 lb, though he has run over today's trip and returns on a reasonable 36-day break.

runners_data.name: Tamzan
runners_data.note: In form winner whose natural inclination is to race from the back — two wins and four places in his last six — but with Drymee and Magic Trip also wanting cover, he is unlikely to find his deepest preferred position; his chance is real on form but the congested rear diminishes how cleanly he can express it.
runners_data.comment: Tamzan won last time out and was third two starts back, but she ranks last on our figures in a field of eight and that gulf makes her very difficult to fancy despite the experience over today's trip and going and a timely 19-day break.

runners_data.name: Glen Nevis
runners_data.note: Six consecutive runs on good ground without a win but consistently placed; William Buick is a significant booking for Charlie Johnston's gelding who races prominently and has strong course form at the trip — he is the type to be thereabouts without necessarily finding enough to win.
runners_data.comment: Glen Nevis shaped with plenty of promise when second last time out and has experience over today's trip and going, with our rating of 81 marking him out as a leading threat; the risk is that he has been winless in his last six starts, and that elusive win remains to be delivered.

races.paceDynamic: Home Hero and Thursday Girl are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over this Sandown mile, creating a genuine, honest gallop rather than a dawdling tactical affair. With Oisin Murphy aboard Thursday Girl and Luke Catton on Home Hero, neither side is likely to concede the rail without a fight, meaning early splits should be true and the race run at a consistent tempo throughout. That honest pace naturally compresses the advantage for pure speed-merchants up front and opens the race to horses capable of travelling smoothly in midfield and picking off the leaders into the straight — a profile that suits Hungarian, Dovecote and Glen Nevis tracking just off the pace. This field contains more hold-up types than the map can comfortably place at the rear; Tamzan, a genuine closer by nature, has been pushed forward to midfield on the map because Drymee and Magic Trip also want cover, meaning the backfield will be crowded and Tamzan is unlikely to secure its preferred deepest berth. The race shape strongly favours the prominent-to-midfield stalker profile — horses who can sit second or third off a genuine gallop and sustain their run from two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Home Hero and Thursday Girl fight for the early lead and set a genuine pace that softens both front-runners entering the straight.
scenarios.body: The honest gallop drains the leaders' reserves in the final furlong, handing the race to horses who travelled smoothly just off the pace and sustain their effort through the Sandown dip. Hungarian, Glen Nevis and Dovecote are all prominent types with good course-relevant form that makes them ideal beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners — most likely Thursday Girl — establishes a clear advantage early and the pace settles into a measured gallop rather than a burn-up.
scenarios.body: Thursday Girl's relentless placed record (four runner-up finishes, one win) and Oisin Murphy's positional intelligence suggest she could control the tempo if Home Hero is unable to match her stride for stride away from the gates. In a soft-pedal scenario from the front, her stamina and consistency at the trip become decisive advantages over closers who fail to get competitive runs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong throughout and the entire prominent group is cooked entering the final two furlongs, leaving a gap for deep closers.
scenarios.body: Drymee has won twice over this trip on good ground and can finish strongly from off the pace, while Magic Trip has the engine for a late thrust if the fractions are truly testing. This scenario demands a true pace meltdown at the front and relies partly on Tamzan being unable to secure a true hold-up berth — making it a less reliable shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Muddle, No Clear Shape
scenarios.trigger: If neither front-runner commits fully, the early pace goes false, and the field concertinas into a bunched mid-race crawl before a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A slow early gallop removes the advantages of the stalker profile and turns the race into a lottery decided by the best turn of foot, favouring horses with raw speed over tactical runners. Glen Nevis's consistent placed record on good ground and Drymee's recent winning form give them the best sprint credentials in a messy finish.

watchPoints.text: Home Hero and Thursday Girl will lock horns for the lead from the stalls — monitor which horse crosses first at the two-furlong mark, as whichever controls the pace controls the shape of the entire race.

Tamzan is a genuine closer who may struggle to find his natural rear position with Drymee and Magic Trip also seeking cover; if all three are in traffic rounding the home turn, a significant late challenge could be compromised.

Home Hero runs just two days after his last start — watch his pre-race demeanour and early exertion; if he is pressured hard by Thursday Girl from the outset having already raced recently, he may empty quickly in the final furlong.

Glen Nevis has William Buick in the saddle, a notable upgrade in jockey quality for a horse that has been placed six times without winning — watch whether Buick gives him a more positive ride from a prominent position than his recent riders have managed.

Hungarian is stepping up from 7f to 8f for the first time and carries tongue-tie; the trip extension is the key unknown — if he stays the mile as well as his pedigree and recent progression suggests, he arrives at the finish with untapped potential.

races.name: Killik Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Post Rider
runners_data.note: Has made the frame on good ground before but recent form reads -73586 and she steps back from longer trips; as the confirmed pace-setter she controls the race shape, yet her trainer has 0 wins from 12 runners over 14 days and her chance may be overstated by her prominent role rather than outright ability.
runners_data.comment: Post Rider has run over today's trip and going before and steps in here with our rating of 76 suggesting she holds clear claims, but she remains winless in her last five starts and will need to find a sharp upturn in form to pose a serious threat.

runners_data.name: Box Clever
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance on good ground 7 days ago (1/8f/GOO) and trainer Portman has one winner from 12 recently; a natural prominent racer who races fresh very well and gets the conditions she wants, making her one of the primary beneficiaries of a steady, lead-controlled tempo.
runners_data.comment: Box Clever makes the perfect reappearance, winning last time out and returning fit just seven days later; she has run over today's distance and going before, and her rating of 80 marks her as the one to beat from stall one carrying 141 lb.

runners_data.name: Dark Rosa
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane takes over for a yard that has one winner from six in the last fortnight; she is by nature a front-rank racer but, with the prominent slots taken, she is likely to be shuffled further back than ideal — her sim-going record of 0 wins from 8 on similar conditions is a further note of caution.
runners_data.comment: Twice third in her last six starts and back in a quick 13 days, Dark Rosa has experience over today's trip and going and our rating of 80 makes her a leading threat at the weights; the risk is she remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Kino Plasmat
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy's booking is the eye-catcher here for Ed Walker, who has 3 winners from 41 runners in the past 14 days; three runs in form (446) suggests inexperience but she has always raced prominently and her profile looks well-suited to sitting just off a controlled pace and improving.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and rated 11 lb below her official mark on our figures, Kino Plasmat looks hard to fancy here, though she has run over today's distance and going before and 23 days since her last outing leaves her fresh enough.

runners_data.name: Poets Praise
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's hold-up filly steps up to a mile for the first time after three starts at 7f, all on soft or standard; 42 days between runs may mean she is cherry-ripe, but the flat Sandown mile on good ground and a single honest pace-setter does not obviously suit a deep closer of her profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, Poets Praise nonetheless catches the eye with her rating of 74 suggesting she holds more ability than her official mark of 68 implies, and she has run over today's trip before; the risk is that her finishes have been modest and 42 days off the track adds an element of doubt.

runners_data.name: Perfect Ruler
runners_data.note: Won on standard ground at a mile but has been held in 5th or worse in her last four starts; she naturally wants to race prominently yet is squeezed out of that position in this shape, racing effectively out of role — Marco Botti has six winners from 23 runners recently, which maintains some interest, but her redistribution tempers expectations materially.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out — just 10 days ago — and has run over today's trip and going, with a trainer firing at 26% over the past fortnight; the weight of 133 lb is the main query, though her rating of 66 suggests she retains ability.

runners_data.name: Dandy Khan
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer by nature whose sim-going record on good is a thin 2 from 15 runs; Pat Cosgrave partners a horse who consistently finishes in the first half of fields without winning — the 8-day turnaround is fine, but the pace shape does not set up the sort of strong finish he needs.
runners_data.comment: Dandy Khan arrives in good nick just eight days after finishing third last time out, and a third two starts back shows consistent form, though she remains winless in recent starts and ranks sixth of eight on our rating.

runners_data.name: Pretty Spirited
runners_data.note: A genuine closer by inclination whose best form has come when getting a true test, but she is displaced into a midfield map position here because the field's rear is equally congested; Alec Voikhansky (claiming allowance of 5lb applies) is an opportunity, and her good-ground form (2/8f/GOO, 3/8f/GOO) is solid, though a controlled tempo is unlikely to produce the late surge her style demands.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of eight on our figures, Pretty Spirited faces a stiff task despite returning in reasonable heart after a second last time out; she has run over today's trip and going before, though little in her recent form suggests she can trouble the leaders here.

races.paceDynamic: Post Rider is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no rival likely to seriously press for the lead on the Sandown mile, she should be able to control tempo from the front on good ground without burning her stamina reserves. Box Clever and Kino Plasmat will track prominently behind her, creating a compact front group but not a truly contested pace — the gallop should be honest rather than fierce, suiting those who can sustain a run rather than those who need a dramatic late injection. The field actually contains more genuine prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: Dark Rosa and Perfect Ruler are natural front-rank horses who are likely to find themselves racing further back than ideal, while Pretty Spirited — a true hold-up filly — is similarly displaced in any midfield projection. With a single uncontested leader and a steady-to-honest pace on good turf over a flat mile, the race shape most favours prominent racers who can travel into the contest and pick up over the final two furlongs, rather than deep closers who need a truly searching gallop to deliver their finishing kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Post Rider Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Post Rider leads at a comfortable pace and the challengers track close enough to pounce in the straight.
scenarios.body: Post Rider sets a sustainable tempo on the Sandown mile, allowing Box Clever and Kino Plasmat to travel smoothly just behind before asserting in the final furlong; good ground on a flat track rewards those who race prominently and can sustain their effort to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Fly Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race and the front group ties up in the final furlong, opening the door for closers.
scenarios.body: Poets Praise and Dandy Khan, racing patiently from hold-up positions, benefit if Post Rider sets a slightly stronger early pace that causes the prominent group to over-race; good ground at Sandown's flat mile does not typically suit pure closers but a fast mid-section could create the gap they need.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Leader Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so gentle that Post Rider is never headed and builds an unassailable lead turning for home.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to make a move early, Post Rider dictates at a crawl before accelerating in the straight and simply stealing the race on the bridle; a soft, uncontested gallop on good turf can flatter a front-runner, though her OR of 69 and recent form suggest she may not be good enough to win a truly muddling race unchallenged.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Reclaim Position
scenarios.trigger: If Dark Rosa or Perfect Ruler manage to secure a forward berth despite the crowded prominent positions and outrun their mapped role.
scenarios.body: Should the early jostling allow one of the natural prominent types to slot in closer to the pace than expected, their strong-travelling style could prove decisive in a race that suits front-rank horses; however, both carry the caveat of racing partially out of their natural position, which statistically reduces their chance of fully expressing their best form.

watchPoints.text: Box Clever: 7 days after a course-and-distance win on identical going, she could use that confidence to track Post Rider and assert decisively — watch if she travels comfortably into the straight.

Dark Rosa and Perfect Ruler: both are natural prominent types who may attempt to push forward at the start despite the congested pace positions — any early jostling for the lead could briefly unsettle the race tempo and create interference risks.

Poets Praise: 42 days off and stepping up in trip to a mile for the first time — if she is rusty from the layoff she may not produce the sustained run her hold-up style demands on what looks like a steady-to-honest pace.

Post Rider: monitor whether she is pressed or completely uncontested in the early stages — the difference between a controlled lead and a truly unchallenged dawdle will materially alter how the straight plays out for the hold-up horses.

Pretty Spirited's 5lb claim with Voikhansky could prove meaningful in a race where weight differences are fine — watch how she is ridden in the first half of the race given she is effectively displaced from her ideal deep hold-up position.

races.name: Killik Family Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Galyx
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Channon; goes well fresh (17 days), but recent similar-going form shows five runs without a win or place, and the STYLE_FIT flag suggests the OR=80 mark may flatter her if she cannot dictate completely unchallenged.
runners_data.comment: Galyx arrives in good nick on 17 days' rest, and his experience over today's trip and going is a solid foundation; our rating of 89 has him top-ranked of the nine, though he was only fourth two starts back and remains winless in recent starts, there is enough here to make him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Sharp Move
runners_data.note: Haggas and Buick is a powerful combination, and the horse's sole turf win came at 10f on Standard; hold-up style suits a stronger pace, so this shape at a controlled tempo is less ideal, but class and stable form merit serious respect.
runners_data.comment: Sharp Move won two starts back but has finished eighth on his most recent outing, and with a speed rating of 72 leaving him ranked seventh of nine on our figures, he looks to have plenty to find against stronger rivals here despite having run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Moon Angel
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with an excellent record on Good ground at 12f — two wins from nine similar-going runs — and a long absence (111 days) is the main query; returns for Williams who has 4/34 over 14 days, suggesting yard is in fair nick.
runners_data.comment: Moon Angel showed a winner two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, but that 111-day absence is a notable query and her latest outing was a well-beaten eighth, leaving her with something to prove on return.

runners_data.name: Carnival Day
runners_data.note: Front-running type for Boyle who has been busy of late (5 runs in recent form); consistent at a prominent pace position but the form string shows no wins, and the OR=75 mark keeps him in the mix rather than ahead of it.
runners_data.comment: Carnival Day arrives here fit on a 16-day turnaround, has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 85 puts him notably ahead of his official mark — a compelling angle for this gelding; yet to win in his last five starts, that winless run is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Sovereign View
runners_data.note: Unexposed three-year-old stepping up significantly in trip from repeated 8f runs on AW; all turf form on Good is sparse (one run, sixth), and the hold-up style means he needs either a strong pace or something to go wrong ahead of him to get involved.
runners_data.comment: Sovereign View has shown admirable consistency in recent starts, finishing in the first four on four of his last five outings, including third last time out, and our rating of 89 marks him as a genuine leading danger; the weight burden of 136 lb is the one factor to overcome.

runners_data.name: Golden Circet
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse at OR=70 whose redistribution to midfield reflects the crowded back of the field — his natural rear-of-the-field style is compressed here; best form has come over further (2nd in a 16f race) and the style compromise tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Golden Circet's best recent effort was a third six starts back, though consecutive fourths two and three starts back suggest consistency without a breakthrough, and he faces a stiff task from draw 9 carrying 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Magnatura
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a visor, whose best form came over 7-11f on Good; the hold-up style and a 28-day absence mean he needs a fast pace to produce his finish, and his recent form (4-0-3-0) is patchy enough to treat with caution.
runners_data.comment: Magnatura showed up well with a third two starts back and has experience over today's trip and going, with our rating of 86 suggesting he merits respect; the concern is that he was unplaced last time out.

runners_data.name: Oh Yes You Do
runners_data.note: Menuisier has 0/5 over 14 days and the horse has been off 48 days; a natural deep closer whose redistribution to a midfield map position means she is unlikely to produce her best, though the underlying 10f form on Good (two wins, two placed) is genuinely strong.
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Oh Yes You Do is hard to fancy despite winning two of her last five starts, with a fifth on her most recent outing 48 days ago doing little to raise confidence; she has run over today's trip and going before, and stall three is her lot at 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Golden Phase
runners_data.note: Murphy takes the ride on this lightly-weighted OR=64 improver who has three wins from 15 Good-ground runs at 10f; stepping up to 12f for the first time at Sandown could prove the stretch too far, but a clever Murphy front-of-the-field ride could see him traffic-free throughout.

races.paceDynamic: Galyx is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no other genuine lead horse to pressure her, she is likely to control this 1m2f contest at a sustainable gallop from the outset. Moon Angel, Carnival Day, and Golden Phase will press forward into prominent positions just behind, creating a small cluster of pace-forward types tracking the leader without turning the race into a genuine test of stamina. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Oh Yes You Do and Golden Circet are true closers who are likely to find themselves racing in a more forward position than natural, reducing the potency of any late surge from the back. This race shape — a controlled, unfussed pace set by one horse — strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader, save ground through the race, and produce a sustained finish over the final two furlongs rather than a sudden burst from deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Galyx Controls, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Galyx leads at a sustainable tempo and the field settles into a well-strung-out shape, allowing those tracking her to quicken in the straight.
scenarios.body: Galyx dictates from the front without being pressured, and the horses tracking her into the home straight get first run on a field that has never genuinely accelerated; Moon Angel's strong Good-ground record at this trip makes her the prime beneficiary, while Carnival Day's consistent front-running profile keeps her competitive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Front Pair Fade
scenarios.trigger: If Moon Angel or Carnival Day push up to pressurise Galyx early, lifting the tempo and turning the race into a stamina test.
scenarios.body: A faster early gallop stretches the field and causes the front pair to tie up late in the straight, opening the door for runners with genuine staying power to come through; Sharp Move and Magnatura, who have both shown the ability to close from off the pace when the pace has been genuine, are best positioned to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong throughout and the front-runners empty inside the final furlong, creating a clear opportunity for hold-up horses to arrive.
scenarios.body: Sharp Move, trained by Haggas and ridden by Buick in a race that sets up with a clear rhythm, would have the quality and late energy to mow down tiring leaders; Oh Yes You Do has the raw form credentials to threaten but is unlikely to secure her natural position, limiting the scenario's probability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, Wide Spread
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling for position disrupts the expected race shape and the field fragments into small groups racing at different paces.
scenarios.body: Without a clean tempo, the race becomes a lottery of positioning and individual ability rather than a test of running style, with Sovereign View's soundness at a shorter trip a concern but Golden Phase's course-and-distance experience offering residual value.

watchPoints.text: Moon Angel is 111 days absent — watch her in the paddock and early in the race for signs of freshness or reluctance to settle, as a tense run after a long layoff could compromise her prominent style entirely.

Oh Yes You Do and Golden Circet, both natural hold-up horses pushed forward on the map, may attempt to drift back to their true position at the start — if they do, watch for traffic issues turning for home in a compacted field.

Galyx's trainer Channon has a 14-day strike rate of just 1/18 and her similar-going form reads five runs without a win or place; if she fails to establish a clear lead from the gates, the entire pace map collapses.

Sharp Move is taking a significant switch from AW (all three recent runs on Tapeta/Standard) back to turf Good — watch the market move for Buick, as any support would suggest confidence the horse handles the surface change.

Golden Phase has Oisin Murphy in the saddle from the lowest OR in the field (64) — watch if Murphy attempts an economy-of-effort front-running ride, which could manufacture a false pace scenario and compress the field earlier than expected.
